context.analysis:
## Overview
- The Library Management System provides cataloging, circulation management, and self-service portals for public and academic libraries.
- The system enforces strict EU-only data residency and maintains a 99th-percentile search response time under 800ms.

## Key Elements
- Library Member (Patron)
- Librarian / Staff
- Library Administrator
- Library Management System (Software System)
- Payment Gateway (External Software System)
- Notification Provider (External Software System)
- Identity Provider (External Software System)

## Relationships
- Users interact with the Library Management System via HTTPS using TLS 1.3.
- Library Management System integrates with Payment Gateway via HTTPS/REST for fine settlements.
- Library Management System integrates with Notification Provider via HTTPS/REST for loan reminders.
- Library Management System authenticates users via Identity Provider using OIDC/OAuth2 over HTTPS.

## Technology Stack
- OIDC/OAuth2: For tiered authentication and user session management.
- TLS 1.3: For encrypted data in transit across all external boundaries.
- AES-256: For data at rest with keys managed in an EU-hosted KMS.
- OpenTelemetry: For centralized distributed tracing to monitor search latency.
- Mutual TLS (mTLS): For Zero Trust inter-container communication.

## Rationale
- Decoupling the public search read-model from the transactional circulation domain ensures the 99th-percentile search response remains under 800ms.
- Strict EU-hosted infrastructure, AES-256 encryption, and vetted regional third-party integrations enforce absolute data residency compliance.

containers.analysis:
## Overview
The Library Management System provides cataloging, circulation management, and self-service portals for public and academic libraries. It enforces strict EU-only data residency and high-performance search capabilities.

## Key Elements
- Library Member (Patron) [person]
- Librarian / Staff [person]
- Library Administrator [person]
- Web Application / SPA [container, React, TypeScript]
- API Gateway [container, NGINX / Envoy]
- Catalog & Search Service [container, Java, Spring Boot + Elasticsearch]
- Circulation Service [container, Node.js / NestJS]
- Database [container, PostgreSQL]
- Message Broker [container, Apache Kafka / RabbitMQ]
- Audit Service [container, Go]
- Payment Gateway [externalSystem]
- Notification Provider [externalSystem]
- Identity Provider [externalSystem]

## Relationships
- Library Member (Patron) -> API Gateway (HTTPS / TLS 1.3)
- Librarian / Staff -> API Gateway (HTTPS / TLS 1.3)
- Library Administrator -> API Gateway (HTTPS / TLS 1.3)
- API Gateway -> Catalog & Search Service (gRPC over mTLS)
- API Gateway -> Circulation Service (gRPC over mTLS)
- Circulation Service -> Message Broker (AMQP/Kafka Protocol over mTLS)
- Circulation Service -> Database (SQL over mTLS)
- Catalog & Search Service -> Database (SQL over mTLS)
- Circulation Service -> Audit Service (REST over mTLS)
- Circulation Service -> Payment Gateway (HTTPS/REST)
- Circulation Service -> Notification Provider (HTTPS/REST)
- API Gateway -> Identity Provider (OIDC/OAuth2 over HTTPS)

## Technology Stack
- React, TypeScript: UI logic for patrons and staff
- NGINX / Envoy: Edge routing, TLS termination, and OIDC token validation
- Java, Spring Boot + Elasticsearch: Dedicated to meeting sub-800ms search and cataloging requirements
- Node.js / NestJS: Manages loans, fines, and business integrations
- PostgreSQL: Primary relational data store for transactional data
- Apache Kafka / RabbitMQ: Asynchronous, event-driven communication
- Go: High-performance audit logging service

## Rationale
Separating the Catalog & Search Service from the Circulation Service guarantees sub-800ms search performance for patrons without risking starvation from staff operations. Deploying all databases and Elasticsearch clusters in EU-only regions with strict mTLS and WORM audit logging ensures complete compliance with data residency and security constraints.

## Key Elements

- Library Administrator

- Notification Provider

- Circulation Service -> Audit Service (REST over mTLS)
- Circulation Service -> Payment Gateway (HTTPS/REST)
- Circulation Service -> Notification Provider (HTTPS/REST)

## Technology Stack
- React, TypeScript: Powers the modern, responsive user interface for patrons and staff.
- NGINX / Envoy: Provides high-performance edge routing, rate limiting, and mTLS termination at the API Gateway.
- Java, Spring Boot + Elasticsearch: Delivers sub-800ms search performance and robust catalog indexing.
- Node.js / NestJS: Manages modular business logic for circulation and fines.
- PostgreSQL: Serves as the reliable primary relational datastore enforcing data integrity.
- Apache Kafka / RabbitMQ: Enables asynchronous, event-driven communication across microservices.
- Go: Powers the high-performance audit logging service for compliance and security tracking.

## Rationale
This architecture uses a secure API Gateway paired with reactive microservices to isolate high-load search and circulation functions, guaranteeing performance SLAs. Strict protocol selection (gRPC over mTLS) and EU-hosted infrastructure fulfill all data residency and security constraints.

Catalog & Search Service.analysis:
## Overview
- Decomposes the Catalog & Search Service for the Library Management System into specialized internal components to deliver sub-800ms search responses and secure cataloging.
- Enforces strict EU-only data residency and role-based access control for all physical and digital inventory operations.

## Key Elements
- Search Query Engine [component] (Java, Spring Data Elasticsearch)
- Catalog Management API [component] (Java, Spring MVC)
- Index Synchronization Worker [component] (Java, Spring Integration)
- Elasticsearch Index [component] (Elasticsearch)
- Database [container] (PostgreSQL)
- API Gateway [container] (NGINX / Envoy)
- Message Broker [container] (Apache Kafka / RabbitMQ)
- Audit Service [container] (Go)

## Relationships
- API Gateway -> Search Query Engine [gRPC over mTLS]
- API Gateway -> Catalog Management API [gRPC over mTLS]
- Search Query Engine -> Elasticsearch Index [Internal Java API / Transport over mTLS]
- Catalog Management API -> Database [SQL over mTLS]
- Index Synchronization Worker -> Message Broker [AMQP/Kafka Protocol over mTLS]
- Index Synchronization Worker -> Database [SQL over mTLS]
- Catalog Management API -> Audit Service [REST over mTLS]

## Technology Stack
- Java & Spring Boot: Core framework for high-performance microservices and component decomposition.
- Elasticsearch: High-speed search engine ensuring 99th-percentile search responses under 800ms.
- PostgreSQL: Relational database providing ACID-compliant transactional persistence.
- Apache Kafka / RabbitMQ: Asynchronous message broker for event-driven index synchronization.
- gRPC & mTLS: Secure, low-latency inter-service communication protocol with mutual TLS authentication.

## Rationale
- Separating the Search Query Engine from the Catalog Management API prevents high-volume patron searches from degrading critical librarian updates.
- Implementing an event-driven Index Synchronization Worker alongside encrypted EU-hosted infrastructure ensures strict data residency, audit compliance, and sub-800ms performance SLAs.

Circulation Service.analysis:
## Overview
- A distributed Library Management System designed to handle public and academic library catalogues, circulation workflows, and self-service portals.
- Enforces strict EU-only data residency while maintaining high-performance search responses under 800 milliseconds at the 99th percentile.

## Key Elements
- Library Member (Patron) [person]
- Librarian / Staff [person]
- Library Administrator [person]
- Web Application / SPA (React, TypeScript) [container]
- API Gateway (NGINX / Envoy) [container]
- Catalog & Search Service (Java, Spring Boot + Elasticsearch) [container]
- Circulation Service (Node.js / NestJS) [container]
- Database (PostgreSQL) [container]
- Message Broker (Apache Kafka / RabbitMQ) [container]
- Audit Service (Go) [container]
- Payment Gateway [externalSystem]
- Notification Provider [externalSystem]
- Identity Provider [externalSystem]

## Relationships
- Library Member (Patron), Librarian / Staff, Library Administrator -> API Gateway: Accesses system features via HTTPS / TLS 1.3
- API Gateway -> Catalog & Search Service, Circulation Service: Routes requests using gRPC over mTLS
- Circulation Service -> Database: Reads and writes transactional data using SQL over mTLS
- Circulation Service -> Message Broker: Publishes and consumes events using AMQP/Kafka Protocol over mTLS
- Circulation Service -> Audit Service: Sends audit logs using REST over mTLS
- Circulation Service -> Payment Gateway, Notification Provider: Processes payments and sends alerts using HTTPS/REST
- API Gateway -> Identity Provider: Authenticates users via OIDC/OAuth2 over HTTPS

## Technology Stack
- React with TypeScript: Powers the Web Application / SPA for client-side rendering.
- NGINX / Envoy: Provides edge routing, TLS termination, and OIDC token validation at the API Gateway.
- Java with Spring Boot & Elasticsearch: Powers the Catalog & Search Service to meet sub-800ms search constraints.
- Node.js with NestJS: Implements the Circulation Service for efficient loan and fine management.
- PostgreSQL: Acts as the primary relational data store with AES-256 PII column encryption.
- Apache Kafka / RabbitMQ: Facilitates asynchronous, event-driven messaging.
- Go: Powers the high-performance Audit Service.
- Kubernetes: Hosts containerized workloads with horizontal pod autoscaling and Vault-backed secrets.

## Rationale
- Microservices architecture cleanly separates high-performance search requirements from transactional circulation workflows.
- Strict mTLS, TLS 1.3, and AES-256 encryption ensure compliance with EU-only data residency and GDPR security mandates.

Database.analysis:
## Overview
The Library Management System provides cataloging, circulation management, and self-service portals for public and academic libraries. The system is designed with a PostgreSQL database container ensuring strict EU-only data residency and sub-800ms search performance.

## Key Elements
- Relational Data Store (PostgreSQL Engine)
- Connection Pooler (PgBouncer)
- Audit Logging Module (pgAudit)
- HA Failover Manager (Patroni)
- Backup & Archival Agent (Barman / WAL-G)
- Circulation Service
- Catalog & Search Service

## Relationships
- Circulation Service -> Connection Pooler: Submits loan and fine transactions [SQL over mTLS]
- Catalog & Search Service -> Connection Pooler: Queries and updates item metadata [SQL over mTLS]
- Connection Pooler -> Relational Data Store: Forwards pooled queries [TCP/IP]
- Relational Data Store -> Audit Logging Module: Emits audit logs [Internal IPC]

## Technology Stack
- PostgreSQL: Provides robust ACID compliance and row-level security for transactional integrity.
- PgBouncer: Manages and optimizes incoming database connections under peak load.
- pgAudit: Captures security-relevant DDL/DML events for compliance.
- Patroni: Handles automated leader election and high availability across availability zones.
- Barman / WAL-G: Manages continuous WAL archiving and point-in-time recovery.

## Rationale
This architecture ensures strict EU-only data residency compliance and high availability for transactional workloads. The component layout protects system stability under heavy academic semester traffic while maintaining data security and PII isolation.

Message Broker.analysis:
## Overview
The Library Management System provides cataloging, circulation management, and self-service portals for public and academic libraries. It enforces strict EU-only data residency and high-performance search capabilities.

## Key Elements
- Library Member (Patron) [person]
- Librarian / Staff [person]
- Library Administrator [person]
- Web Application / SPA (React, TypeScript) [container]
- API Gateway (NGINX / Envoy) [container]
- Catalog & Search Service (Java, Spring Boot + Elasticsearch) [container]
- Circulation Service (Node.js / NestJS) [container]
- Database (PostgreSQL) [container]
- Message Broker (Apache Kafka) [container]
- Audit Service (Go) [container]
- Payment Gateway [externalSystem]
- Notification Provider [externalSystem]
- Identity Provider [externalSystem]

## Relationships
- Library Member (Patron), Librarian / Staff, Library Administrator -> API Gateway [HTTPS / TLS 1.3]
- API Gateway -> Catalog & Search Service [gRPC over mTLS]
- API Gateway -> Circulation Service [gRPC over mTLS]
- Circulation Service -> Message Broker [AMQP/Kafka Protocol over mTLS]
- Catalog & Search Service -> Message Broker [Kafka Protocol over mTLS]
- Audit Service -> Message Broker [Kafka Protocol over mTLS]
- Circulation Service -> Database [SQL over mTLS]
- Catalog & Search Service -> Database [SQL over mTLS]
- Circulation Service -> Audit Service [REST over mTLS]
- Circulation Service -> Payment Gateway [HTTPS/REST]
- Circulation Service -> Notification Provider [HTTPS/REST]
- API Gateway -> Identity Provider [OIDC/OAuth2 over HTTPS]

## Technology Stack
- React, TypeScript: Responsive and type-safe user interface for patrons and staff.
- NGINX / Envoy: Edge routing, TLS termination, and OIDC token validation.
- Java, Spring Boot + Elasticsearch: High-performance cataloging and sub-800ms search fulfillment.
- Node.js / NestJS: Scalable business logic handling loans and fine management.
- PostgreSQL: Robust relational storage for transactional data integrity.
- Apache Kafka: Persistent, event-driven message broker supporting dead-letter queues and EU data residency.
- Go: High-performance audit logging for security compliance.

## Rationale
The architecture decouples high-frequency catalog searches from transactional circulation flows using asynchronous messaging. This ensures sub-800ms search response times and strict EU-only data residency compliance.

Audit Service.analysis:
## Overview
The Library Management System is a comprehensive digital solution for public and academic libraries designed to catalogue items, manage circulation, and provide self-service portals. It enforces strict EU-only data residency and sub-800ms search performance requirements.

## Key Elements
- Library Member (Patron) [person]
- Librarian / Staff [person]
- Library Administrator [person]
- Web Application / SPA (React, TypeScript) [container]
- API Gateway (NGINX / Envoy) [container]
- Catalog & Search Service (Java, Spring Boot + Elasticsearch) [container]
- Circulation Service (Node.js / NestJS) [container]
- Message Broker (Apache Kafka / RabbitMQ) [container]
- Audit Service (Go) [container]
  - Audit Consumer [component, Go]
  - Audit API Handler [component, Go]
  - Audit Database (PostgreSQL) [component]
- Identity Provider, Payment Gateway, Notification Provider [externalSystem]

## Relationships
- Library Member (Patron), Librarian / Staff, Library Administrator -> API Gateway (HTTPS / TLS 1.3)
- API Gateway -> Catalog & Search Service (gRPC over mTLS)
- API Gateway -> Circulation Service (gRPC over mTLS)
- API Gateway -> Audit API Handler (gRPC over mTLS)
- Circulation Service, Catalog & Search Service -> Message Broker (AMQP/Kafka Protocol over mTLS)
- Message Broker -> Audit Consumer (AMQP/Kafka Protocol over mTLS)
- Audit Consumer, Audit API Handler -> Audit Database (SQL over mTLS)
- API Gateway -> Identity Provider (OIDC/OAuth2 over HTTPS)

## Technology Stack
- Go: Chosen for the Audit Service to deliver high-performance, low-latency event processing.
- Java & Elasticsearch: Powers the Catalog & Search Service to meet sub-800ms performance constraints.
- PostgreSQL: Serves as the primary transactional database and immutable audit data store with EU data residency.
- Apache Kafka / RabbitMQ: Enables asynchronous, decoupled event-driven communication and dead-letter queue reliability.
- React & TypeScript: Delivers modern, responsive UI logic for the Web Application SPA.

## Rationale
This architecture decouples core transactions from logging via a message broker to protect patron-facing performance. It enforces regulatory compliance, GDPR adherence, and security via strict EU data residency, mTLS transport, and RBAC-secured audit exports.
